The argument takes place on the fixed classical and synthetic sphere systems. It reduces the last possible differential on $h_6^2$ to three detection conditions, proves that two of these conditions cannot hold together, and concludes nonzero permanence.
In the statements quoted from \cite{LWX126}, spectra are assumed to be $2$-completed, connective, and of finite type. The original statements and their context are in \href{paper/main.tex.html}{the article source} and \href{paper/2412.10879.pdf}{the article PDF}.

blocks.title: The fixed sphere and its obstruction classes

blocks.tex:
Let $E_r^{s,t}$ be the classical Adams spectral sequence of the sphere from Chapter 2, with stem $t-s$. Write $S^{0,0}$ for the synthetic sphere, with its quotient maps, comparison maps and convergence filtration, and set
\[
 W=x_{126,8,4}+x_{126,8},\qquad U=h_0^2x_{124,8},\qquad T=h_1h_4x_{109,12}.
\]
Here the classes are as in Chapter 4. A class $x$ detects a homotopy class $a$ when the image of $a$ in the corresponding associated graded quotient equals the image of $x$.

\textit{(From \cite{LWX126}, Corollary 1.5.)}

\]

\[
 C\;:\!\Longleftrightarrow\;\forall t\in\mathbb Z\ \forall x\in E_2^{2,t},\quad
 x\text{ survives nontrivially to }E_\infty\ \Longleftrightarrow\ L(t,x).
\]
This entry defines the target; it does not prove $C$.

blocks.label: sem:Main:remark-7.4
blocks.title: Remark 7.4: normalization of the finite-quotient criterion
blocks.body:
\textit{(From \cite{LWX126}, Remark 7.4.)}
Let $q_n$ denote the quotient map to $S^{0,0}/\lambda^n$. For every $a\in\pi_{125,130}S^{0,0}$ and $n\geq0$,
\[
 q_n(a)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q_{n+1}(\lambda a)=0.
\]
In particular, with $a=\eta(\theta_5^{\mathrm{BX}})^2$ this identifies the two quotient conditions
\[
 q_r\bigl(\eta(\theta_5^{\mathrm{BX}})^2\bigr)=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 q_{r+1}\bigl(\lambda\eta(\theta_5^{\mathrm{BX}})^2\bigr)=0.
\]
\par\emph{Proof.} Exactness of the lambda cofiber sequence identifies $\ker q_n$ with the image of $\lambda^n$. Multiplication by $\lambda$ is injective on $\pi_{125,130}S^{0,0}$ in the fixed system. Thus $\lambda a=\lambda^{n+1}b$ is equivalent to $a=\lambda^n b$. Specializing $a$ gives the change of quotient convention used in \ref{paper:7.3}.



\href{paper/main.tex.html#L2127}{Original remark}.

blocks.label: sem:Main:remark-7.5
blocks.title: Remark 7.5: independence of the theta choice
blocks.body:
\textit{(From \cite{LWX126}, Remark 7.5.)}
For every $\theta\in\pi_{62,64}S^{0,0}$ satisfying $\operatorname{ThetaChoice}(\theta)$,
\[
 \lambda\eta\theta^2=\lambda\eta(\theta_5^{\mathrm{BX}})^2.
\]
In particular, this expression has the same value for any two admissible choices. It is the expression, rather than $\theta$ itself, that is independent of the choice.
\par\emph{Proof.} The stem-62 choice comparison places $\theta-\theta_5^{\mathrm{BX}}$ in filtration at least six. The exponent-two square identity therefore puts $\theta^2-(\theta_5^{\mathrm{BX}})^2$ in filtration at least twelve. The established eta-error estimate raises the filtration of its eta multiple to at least fifteen. This eta-product difference is annihilated by two and has zero detector image, so the established filtration-fifteen detection theorem makes it zero. Multiplying by $\lambda$ gives the claimed equality.



\href{paper/main.tex.html#L2133}{Original remark}.

public theorem lambda_eta_theta_square_independent
    (theta : BiHom 62 64 (S_0_0 : SyntheticSpectrum)) (htheta : ThetaChoice theta) :
    KIP126.Literature.Standard.lambdaEtaThetaSquare theta =
      KIP126.Literature.Standard.lambdaEtaThetaSquare
        KIP126.Literature.Standard.bxTheta5 := by
  classical
  let theta' := KIP126.Literature.Standard.bxTheta5
  have hgap := Internal.Choice.theta_choice_filtration_gap_of_pages
    Internal.Choice.theta_choice_finite_pages theta theta' htheta
    KIP126.Literature.Standard.bx_theta_label
  have hsquare : FiltrationAtLeast model.syntheticTower 12
      (sphereProduct theta theta - sphereProduct theta' theta') := by
    rw [Internal.Choice.theta_square_difference theta theta'
      KIP126.Literature.Standard.bx_order_two]
    exact KIP126.Literature.Standard.action_filtration .sphere 62 64 62 64 6 6
      (theta-theta') (theta-theta') hgap hgap
  have herror := Internal.Selected.eta_weight128_branches_filtration_fifteen _
    (Internal.Selected.stem124_weight128_filtration11_branches
      (Internal.Selected.theta_sphere_frame 13 137 9 (by decide) (by decide) _
        Internal.Selected.correction_infinity_generated) _
      (model.syntheticTower.filtrationSubmodule_antitone _ (124,128)
        (by decide : (11:ℤ) ≤ 12) hsquare))
  have hlinear : sphereProduct KIP126.Literature.Standard.eta
      (sphereProduct theta theta - sphereProduct theta' theta') =
      sphereProduct KIP126.Literature.Standard.eta (sphereProduct theta theta) -
        sphereProduct KIP126.Literature.Standard.eta (sphereProduct theta' theta') := by
    simp only [sphereProduct, Int.reduceAdd, CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_sub]
  rw [hlinear] at herror
  have heq := Internal.High125.detector_injective_filtration15 _ herror
    (Internal.High125.eta_product_difference_order_two 124 128
      (sphereProduct theta theta) (sphereProduct theta' theta')) (by
    rw [CategoryTheory.Preadditive.sub_comp,
      Internal.High125.synthetic_eta_theta_square_detector_zero theta,
      Internal.High125.synthetic_eta_theta_square_detector_zero theta', sub_self])
  have h := congrArg (lambdaMultiply 1) (sub_eq_zero.mp heq)
  exact h

blocks.label: sem:Main:any-choice-criterion
blocks.title: Normalization and choice transport of the literature criterion
blocks.body:
\textit{(From \cite{LWX126}, Theorem 7.3 and Remarks 7.4--7.5; \cite{BurklundXu}, Proposition 7.19.)}
The literature criterion is recalled in \ref{paper:7.3}. On the fixed system its normalized form is as follows.
For every admissible $\theta$ and every natural number $r\geq0$,
\[
 h_6^2\text{ survives to }E_{r+3}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 [\lambda\eta\theta^2]=0\text{ in }S^{0,0}/\lambda^{r+1}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 P\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\lambda\eta\theta^2=0
 \text{ in the untruncated synthetic sphere}.
\]
\par\emph{Proof.} For $r\geq1$, apply the distinguished-choice literature criterion and then combine \ref{sem:Main:remark-7.4} with \ref{sem:Main:remark-7.5}. At $r=0$, $h_6^2$ survives to $E_3$ and every lambda multiple maps to zero in $S^{0,0}/\lambda$. The untruncated equivalence is the distinguished-choice literature criterion followed by \ref{sem:Main:remark-7.5}.

lean.code:
public theorem any_choice_criterion
    (theta : BiHom 62 64 (S_0_0 : SyntheticSpectrum)) (htheta : ThetaChoice theta) :
    (∀ r : ℕ,
      (SurvivesTo model.classical.sphere ((r : ℤ)+3) (2,128)
        model.standardClasses.standardH6Square ↔
        quotientClass (r+1) (KIP126.Literature.Standard.lambdaEtaThetaSquare theta) = 0)) ∧
    (H6SquarePermanent ↔ KIP126.Literature.Standard.lambdaEtaThetaSquare theta = 0) := by
  have he := lambda_eta_theta_square_independent theta htheta
  constructor
  · intro r
    cases r with
    | zero =>
      exact ⟨fun _ => lambda_eta_theta_square_mod_lambda_zero theta,
        fun _ => h6_square_survives_three⟩
    | succ r =>
      rw [he]
      exact normalized_bx_finite (r+1) (by omega)
  · rw [he]
    exact KIP126.Literature.Standard.bx_untruncated

blocks.label: paper:1.5
blocks.title: Survivors on the Adams 2-line
blocks.body:
\textit{(From \cite{LWX126}, Corollary 1.5.)}
                          

    On the Adams 2-line, the only non-trivial elements that survive in the Adams spectral sequence are:
    $$h_0h_2, \ h_0h_3, \ h_2h_4, \ h_1h_j \ (j \geq 3), \ h_j^2 \ (j \leq 6).$$
                        
                                                                                                                                


\par\emph{Proof.} Write any nonzero second-line class as a standard product using the exhaustive $E_2$ basis. Its third-page continuation restricts it to the corrected Adams--Lin--Leibniz candidates, including $h_0h_4$. Four exceptional mixed products support nonzero outgoing differentials, while HHR excludes squares of index at least seven. Conversely, the remaining products survive by the low-dimensional, Mahowald-family and Kervaire literature inputs, together with the main $h_6^2$ theorem.

  constructor
  · intro hx
    obtain ⟨i,j,hij,degree,heq⟩ := KIP126.E2Computation.two_line_exhaustive t x
      (survival_nonzero hx)
    have hp := (survival_regrade degree (KIP126.Literature.Standard.hiProduct i j)).mp

    exact ⟨i,j,surviving_pair_listed i j hij hp,degree,heq⟩
  · rintro ⟨i,j,hij,degree,heq⟩
    rw [heq]
    exact (survival_regrade degree (KIP126.Literature.Standard.hiProduct i j)).mpr
      (listed_pair_survives i j hij)

blocks.label: paper:7.8
blocks.title: The last differential and its detection conditions
blocks.body:
\textit{(From \cite{LWX126}, Proposition 7.8.)}
                          

Exactly one of the following two statements is true:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(1)] The element $h_6^2$ survives to the $E_\infty$-page.
   
    \item[(2)] There is a nonzero classical Adams differential 
    $$d_{12}(h_6^2) = h_1h_4x_{109,12}.$$
\end{enumerate}
Furthermore, statement $(2)$ is true if and only if the following three statements are all true:
\begin{enumerate} 
    \item[(3)] \leavevmode  
    $$d_6(x_{126,8,4} + x_{126,8}) = 0.$$
    
    \item[(4)] There exists a $\theta_5$ such that 
    $\theta_5^2$ is detected by $\lambda^6 h_0^2x_{124,8}$. In particular, 
    $$\theta_5^2 = \lambda^6 [h_0^2x_{124,8}] \neq 0 \in \pi_{124,124+4}S^{0,0}$$
    for some $[h_0^2x_{124,8}]$.

    \item[(5)] There exists a homotopy class $[h_0^2x_{124,8}]$ such that
    $\lambda^3 \eta [h_0^2x_{124,8}]$ is detected by $\lambda^6 h_1h_4x_{109,12}$. In particular, we have 
    $$\lambda^3 \eta [h_0^2x_{124,8}] = \lambda^6 [h_1h_4x_{109,12}] \in \pi_{125,125+8} S^{0,0}$$
    for some $[h_1h_4x_{109,12}]$.
\end{enumerate}
